# Project glue

<!-- Generated by the chisel setup questionnaire (sections A–H below). This
file is the GLUE: the single indirection point the discipline, the workflow
and the skills read to resolve project-specific paths and behaviour.
`init` writes it once from the questionnaire answers below (each pre-filled
with its default); `update` re-renders the managed parts of the socle but never
touches this file.

Its personal counterpart is `.agents/user.md` — one per dev, never committed,
posed from `.agents/user.md.tpl`. A fact everyone's agents need belongs HERE;
a fact true of one machine or one account belongs there. -->

## A · Task workspace

<!-- Questionnaire asks: where do tasks, archive, journal, roadmap, and the
two task templates live? Default is root `/project-management/`; an
Astro-embedded variant may nest it elsewhere.

The journal line is the ONE place the journal's path is declared: everything
that writes to it — the workflow, the skills — resolves through this line
and never hardcodes a name. Its default is `JOURNAL.md`, a name no other
document claims: a repo's `CHANGELOG.md` belongs to its releases, and this
is a different document. A repo equipped under an older name (`CHANGELOG.md`,
then `LOG.md`) keeps working with that name here; the `chisel-upgrade` skill
renames it.

That journal is WRITTEN BY HAND — one dated entry per task, added by the agent
at the end of the work. It is never generated: not from a tracker's audit
trail, not from the git history, not from anything else. It is
narration, and narration nobody wrote is worth nothing to the next reader.
Architecture decision records are a separate artifact and none of this touches
them. -->

- **Tasks root:** `/project-management/`
- **Tasks:** `/project-management/tasks/`
- **Archive:** `/project-management/archive/`
- **Journal:** `/project-management/JOURNAL.md`
- **Roadmap:** `/project-management/ROADMAP.md`
- **Spec template:** `/project-management/000-template.spec.md`
- **Work template:** `/project-management/000-template.work.md`
- **Task id script:** `/scripts/task-id.sh`

## B · Tracker

<!-- Questionnaire asks: where do your tasks live, and what reads and updates
them? Everything that reads or writes a task's status resolves through this
section and never hardcodes a tool. Whatever the tracker, the spec and work
documents live in the task workspace of Section A, and the tracker item
points at the spec document. The tracker maps the seven statuses of
`.agents/workflow.md` ("Statuses") onto its own states, in the skill or tool
named below.

The usual answers, and what this section says for each:

- **the task files** (the default): the `**Status:**` line of each spec
  document, edited by hand. Nothing to install.
- **beads**, a status database committed next to the files: read and updated
  with `.agents/skills/chisel-beads/SKILL.md`. Each spec's status line
  becomes `**Status:** tracked as <id>`.
- **Plane**, GitHub Issues or another tool: read and updated with its MCP
  server or its skill, named on the line below; the link back to the spec
  document is written in the tracker item. Adding a tracker is naming its
  tool here: no change to the toolkit. -->

- **Tasks live in:** the task files of Section A
- **Read and updated with:** the `**Status:**` line of each spec document,
  edited by hand
- **Link back:** _(none — the task files are the tracker)_

## C · Reading list

<!-- Questionnaire asks: what should a fresh agent session read at start, to
load context cheaply? Boilerplate projects get this prefilled; brownfield
repos get scanned and the list built with assistance. -->

- `README.md`
- `<Journal>` (see Section A) — most recent entries
- `docs/constitution.md` — project principles (carried over from Spec Kit)
- `docs/agent-rules/common.md` — TypeScript and naming conventions
- `docs/agent-rules/git-workflow.md` — gitmoji commits, branch naming, PR
  format
- History of the Spec Kit era: `project-management/archive/speckit-*/`
  (read only when a task reopens one of those features)

## D · Documentation reference

<!-- Questionnaire asks: where do the living, evergreen docs (as-built
architecture, domain pages) live, outside the task workspace? -->

- **Living docs root:** `docs/**` (outside the task workspace declared in
  Section A)
- **Architecture index:** `docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the page the
  close step of `.agents/workflow.md` starts a promotion from. Not written
  yet: the first task that needs it creates it, seeded from the
  "Architecture Overview" of `CLAUDE.md`.

## E · Adapters

questionnaire directly. -->

- [x] `AGENTS.md` (source of truth, managed block)
- [x] `CLAUDE.md` (`@AGENTS.md` import)
- [x] `.claude/skills` → `.agents/skills` (symlink)

## F · Gate commands

<!-- Questionnaire asks: lint / test / build / browser-check commands,
prefilled from repo exploration + package.json where possible. -->

- **Lint:** `pnpm lint` (read-only in every package; each package's
  `pnpm lint:fix` applies the auto-fixes)
- **Typecheck:** `pnpm typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` in every package, test
  files included; mobile route types are only as fresh as the last
  `expo start`, which writes the gitignored `.expo/types`)
- **Test:** `pnpm test`
- **Build:** `pnpm build`
- **Browser check:** `cd apps/mobile && pnpm web` + manual check (needs
  `pnpm db:up` and `pnpm dev:api` running)

## G · Glossary & decisions

<!-- Questionnaire asks: where does the domain glossary live, and where are
ADRs recorded? Decisions LINK existing rationale — never duplicate it. -->

- **Glossary:** `docs/CONTEXT.md` (not written yet — created by the first
  task that needs it, with the `domain-modeling` skill)
- **ADRs:** `docs/adr/`
